        let index_path = cqs_dir.join(cqs::INDEX_DB_FILENAME);
        let store = Store::open_readonly_after_init(&index_path, |_| Ok(())).expect("ro store");
        let result = build_hnsw_base_index(&store, &cqs_dir, None, None).expect("must not error");
        assert_eq!(
            result,
            Some((n, cqs::hnsw::SaveOutcome::Saved)),

pub fn load_with_dim(dir: &Path, basename: &str, dim: usize) -> Result<Self, HnswError> {
        let _span = tracing::debug_span!("hnsw_load", dir = %dir.display(), basename).entered();

        // The stale-temp cleanup, the manifest read, and the existence check
        // all happen INSIDE the shared-lock critical section.
        //
        // Cleanup before the lock would race a concurrent `save()`: pre-lock,
        // a loader could `remove_dir_all` a leftover temp while a saver is
        // mid-flight. Once the shared lock is held, no exclusive saver is
        // in-flight, so any surviving `.tmp` entry is genuinely stale.
        //
        // Reading the manifest and checking existence before the lock would
        // open a TOCTOU window: a concurrent `save()` could commit a new
        // manifest generation and GC the old artifacts out from under a
        // pre-lock reader. The manifest commit (`atomic_replace`) and the
        // generation GC both require the exclusive lock, so holding the shared
        // lock across resolve-then-load pins one generation for the load.
        //
        // The generation scheme closes the old half-replaced-set hazard
        // outright: the current generation is whatever the manifest points at,
        // its artifacts are written under a fresh generation name before the
        // pointer flips, and superseded artifacts are GC'd only after. A load
        // never observes a partially-replaced set — only a whole generation or
        // none.

        // Acquire shared lock for the read phase only (released before
        // return). Protects the on-disk artifact files from being replaced by
        // a concurrent `save()` while this function is reading them — once the
        // data is in memory the copy is independent and the lock is no longer
        // needed.
        //
        // NOTE: File locking is advisory only on WSL over 9P. The lock
        // is best-effort cross-process; an external Windows tool can
        // still modify the files.
        //
        // **Why the lock must NOT outlive the read phase**: keeping the
        // shared lock alive for the index's entire lifetime (by storing
        // it on the returned `HnswIndex`) deadlocks the daemon. The same
        // process's HNSW rebuild thread calls `save()` from a *second*
        // file descriptor on the same lock path; Linux `flock(2)`'s
        // exclusive-waits-for-shared-even-self semantics block the
        // rebuild thread permanently. Dropping the lock at the bottom of
        // this function makes the load and save paths use disjoint open
        // descriptions so the in-process self-deadlock can't form.
        // Cross-process exclusion during runtime is theoretical anyway —
        // concurrent writers race on the SQLite writer lock first.
        let lock_path = dir.join(format!("{}.hnsw.lock", basename));
        let lock_file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
            .read(true)
            .write(true)
            .create(true)
            .truncate(false)
            .open(&lock_path)?;
        // Bound the wait with try-lock-and-retry so a wedged peer process
        // holding the exclusive save lock doesn't hang every reader
        // indefinitely. 5 attempts × 200 ms (with jitter) = ~1s ceiling;
        // daemons can retry the load and CLI users see a clear error
        // instead of a silent hang. Without this, a paused `cqs index`
        // (debugger / SIGSTOP) takes down all readers.
        let lock_acquired = (0..5).any(|attempt| {
            if attempt > 0 {
                let jitter = std::time::Duration::from_millis(200 + (attempt * 37) as u64);
                std::thread::sleep(jitter);
            }
            lock_file.try_lock_shared().is_ok()
        });
        if !lock_acquired {
            return Err(HnswError::Internal(format!(
                "HNSW load lock contended after 5 retries — concurrent save in progress at {}",
                lock_path.display()
            )));
        }
        warn_wsl_advisory_locking(dir);
        tracing::debug!(lock_path = %lock_path.display(), "Acquired HNSW load lock (shared, released after read)");

        // Clean up stale temps from interrupted saves. This runs under the
        // shared lock: a live `save()` holds the exclusive lock while it
        // writes, so any `.tmp` entry observed here is from a crashed/killed
        // save and safe to remove. Temps carry an unpredictable suffix, so
        // match by prefix+suffix. Two shapes: a legacy staging directory, and
        // the manifest-commit temp file left by a crash mid-`atomic_replace`.
        if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
            let prefix = format!(".{}.", basename);
            for entry in entries.flatten() {
                let name = entry.file_name();
                let name = name.to_string_lossy();
                if name.starts_with(&prefix) && name.ends_with(".tmp") {
                    tracing::info!(dir = %entry.path().display(), "Cleaning up interrupted HNSW save");

pub(crate) fn build_hnsw_index_owned<M>(
    store: &cqs::store::Store<M>,
    cqs_dir: &Path,
    cancel: Option<&std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>,
    skip_save: Option<&dyn Fn() -> bool>,
) -> Result<
    Option<(
        HnswIndex,
        std::collections::HashSet<u64>,
        cqs::hnsw::SaveOutcome,
    )>,
> {
    // Capture the store-state stamp BEFORE streaming embeddings: it names
    // the store state the built index reflects. `save_stamped` re-reads the
    // live stamp under the exclusive save lock and discards the save if the
    // store moved past this snapshot.
    let snapshot = cqs::hnsw::StoreStamp::read(store)
        .context("Failed to read store stamp before HNSW build")?;
    let chunk_count = snapshot.chunk_count as usize;
    let _span = tracing::info_span!("build_hnsw_index_owned", chunk_count).entered();

    if chunk_count == 0 {
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let batch_size = hnsw_batch_size(store.dim());

    // Tee the (id, embedding, hash) stream: HNSW build consumes
    // (id, embedding) pairs while we accumulate fingerprints into a side
    // set. Single SQL pass — no second query, no risk of the hash drifting
    // from the embedding under concurrent writers.
    let mut snapshot_keys: std::collections::HashSet<u64> =
        std::collections::HashSet::with_capacity(chunk_count);
    let chunk_batches = store.embedding_and_hash_batches(batch_size).map(|batch| {
        batch.map(|triples| {
            let mut pairs = Vec::with_capacity(triples.len());
            for (id, emb, hash) in triples {
                snapshot_keys.insert(snapshot_fingerprint(&id, &hash));
                pairs.push((id, emb));
            }
            pairs
        })
    });

    let hnsw = HnswIndex::build_batched_with_dim(chunk_batches, chunk_count, store.dim())?;
    // Shutdown check before entering the save: daemon exit detaches the
    // rebuild thread after a bounded join, so a save started after the
    // shutdown signal could be killed at an arbitrary point. Skipping it
    // leaves the dirty flag set and the previous on-disk index intact —
    // the next daemon start rebuilds.
    if cancel
        .map(|c| c.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire))
        .unwrap_or(false)
    {
        anyhow::bail!("shutdown requested — skipping HNSW save (next start rebuilds)");
    }
    // Skip the save when the caller's identity guard reports the backing DB was
    // replaced since this build began (a concurrent `cqs index --force`). This
    // `store` is orphaned on the old inode, so `save_stamped`'s under-lock stamp
    // re-read cannot see the replacement and would overwrite its fresh sidecar
    // with this stale build. Report `DiscardedStale` (the existing stale
    // variant) and still return the built index — the caller decides whether to
    // swap it, and the dirty flag stays set so the next rebuild recovers.
    if skip_save.map(|f| f()).unwrap_or(false) {
        return Ok(Some((
            hnsw,
            snapshot_keys,
            cqs::hnsw::SaveOutcome::DiscardedStale,
        )));
    }
    let outcome = hnsw.save_stamped(cqs_dir, "index", store, snapshot)?;

    Ok(Some((hnsw, snapshot_keys, outcome)))
}

pub(crate) fn build_hnsw_base_index<M>(
    store: &cqs::store::Store<M>,
    cqs_dir: &Path,
    cancel: Option<&std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>,
    skip_save: Option<&dyn Fn() -> bool>,
) -> Result<Option<(usize, cqs::hnsw::SaveOutcome)>> {
    let _span = tracing::info_span!("build_hnsw_base_index").entered();

    // Stamp captured before streaming — see `build_hnsw_index_owned`. The
    // base index is sized by `base_embedding_count`, but the stamp is the
    // store-level state (chunk count + write generation) like the enriched
    // one: it names a point in the store's history, not the row subset.
    let snapshot = cqs::hnsw::StoreStamp::read(store)
        .context("Failed to read store stamp before base HNSW build")?;

    // If the column hasn't been populated yet, skip the build so we don't
    // write an empty HNSW file that misleads readers into thinking dual
    // indexing is active.
    let base_count = store
        .base_embedding_count()
        .context("Failed to count rows with embedding_base")? as usize;

    if base_count == 0 {
        tracing::info!("No embedding_base rows yet — skipping base HNSW build");
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let batch_size = hnsw_batch_size(store.dim());

    let chunk_batches = store.embedding_base_batches(batch_size);
    let hnsw = HnswIndex::build_batched_with_dim(chunk_batches, base_count, store.dim())?;
    // Shutdown check before entering the save — see `build_hnsw_index_owned`.
    if cancel
        .map(|c| c.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire))
        .unwrap_or(false)
    {
        anyhow::bail!("shutdown requested — skipping base HNSW save (next start rebuilds)");
    }
    // Skip the save when the DB was replaced since this build began — same
    // orphaned-handle reasoning as `build_hnsw_index_owned`.
    if skip_save.map(|f| f()).unwrap_or(false) {
        return Ok(Some((hnsw.len(), cqs::hnsw::SaveOutcome::DiscardedStale)));
    }
    let outcome = hnsw.save_stamped(cqs_dir, "index_base", store, snapshot)?;

    tracing::info!(base_count, ?outcome, "Base HNSW index built");
    Ok(Some((hnsw.len(), outcome)))
}

fn is_external_trait_method(entry: &DeadFunction) -> bool {
    /// Framework-dispatched Rust trait methods. Held as an explicit set (not a
    /// name-shape rule) so the excuse never widens past methods known to be
    /// invoked by a runtime/framework rather than a syntactic call. The serde
    /// names are the full `Visitor` trait surface (serde 1.0).
    const EXTERNAL_TRAIT_METHODS: &[&str] = &[
        // serde `Visitor` family.
        "expecting",
        "visit_bool",
        "visit_i8",
        "visit_i16",
        "visit_i32",
        "visit_i64",
        "visit_i128",
        "visit_u8",
        "visit_u16",
        "visit_u32",
        "visit_u64",
        "visit_u128",
        "visit_f32",
        "visit_f64",
        "visit_char",
        "visit_str",
        "visit_borrowed_str",
        "visit_string",
        "visit_bytes",
        "visit_borrowed_bytes",
        "visit_byte_buf",
        "visit_none",
        "visit_some",
        "visit_unit",
        "visit_newtype_struct",
        "visit_seq",
        "visit_map",
        "visit_enum",
        // hnsw_rs `FilterT`.
        "hnsw_filter",
    ];
    let lang = entry.chunk.language.to_string();
    let name = entry.chunk.name.as_str();
    // Robust structural gate: only a real trait-impl method (`ChunkType::Method`)
    // is excused. A free function (`ChunkType::Function`) sharing the name is not
    // framework-dispatched and stays `dead`.
    entry.chunk.chunk_type == cqs::parser::ChunkType::Method
        && lang == "rust"
        && EXTERNAL_TRAIT_METHODS.contains(&name)
}

fn extract_container_name_rust_rust(container: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if container.kind() == "impl_item" {
        container.child_by_field_name("type").and_then(|t| {
            if t.kind() == "type_identifier" {
                Some(source[t.byte_range()].to_string())
            } else {
                // generic_type wraps type_identifier: Foo<T>
                let mut cursor = t.walk();
                for child in t.children(&mut cursor) {
                    if child.kind() == "type_identifier" {
                        return Some(source[child.byte_range()].to_string());
                    }
                }
                None
            }
        })
    } else {
        // trait_item: read "name" field
        container
            .child_by_field_name("name")
            .map(|n| source[n.byte_range()].to_string())
    }
}

fn post_process_rust_rust(
    name: &mut String,
    chunk_type: &mut ChunkType,
    node: tree_sitter::Node,
    source: &str,
) -> bool {
    // Drop expression-position macro invocations (e.g. `println!` in a fn body):
    // only item-scope invocations anchor a MacroInvocation chunk. See
    // `is_item_scope_macro_invocation`.
    if *chunk_type == ChunkType::MacroInvocation && !is_item_scope_macro_invocation(node) {
        return false;
    }

    // Rust convention: fn new(...) inside an impl block is a constructor
    if *chunk_type == ChunkType::Method && name == "new" {
        *chunk_type = ChunkType::Constructor;
    }

    // #[test] functions → Test chunk type
    // In tree-sitter-rust, attribute_item is a sibling before the function_item
    if *chunk_type == ChunkType::Function || *chunk_type == ChunkType::Method {
        let mut sibling = node.prev_sibling();
        while let Some(sib) = sibling {
            if sib.kind() == "attribute_item" {
                let attr_text = &source[sib.byte_range()];
                if attr_text.contains("#[test]") || attr_text.contains("#[tokio::test]") {
                    *chunk_type = ChunkType::Test;
                    break;
                }
            } else if sib.kind() != "line_comment" && sib.kind() != "block_comment" {
                break; // stop at non-attribute, non-comment siblings
            }
            sibling = sib.prev_sibling();
        }
    }

    // static mut → Variable (mutable, not constant)
    if *chunk_type == ChunkType::Constant && node.kind() == "static_item" {
        let text = &source[node.byte_range()];
        if text.contains("static mut ") {
            *chunk_type = ChunkType::Variable;
        }
    }

    // Functions inside extern blocks → Extern
    if *chunk_type == ChunkType::Function {
        let mut parent = node.parent();
        while let Some(p) = parent {
            if p.kind() == "extern_block" || p.kind() == "foreign_mod_item" {
                *chunk_type = ChunkType::Extern;
                break;
            }
            parent = p.parent();
        }
    }

    true
}

pub fn open(rt: &Runtime, index_path: &Path) -> Option<Self> {
        use sqlx::ConnectOptions;
        let result = rt.block_on(async {
            // Mirror the Store's read-only open shape (filename + read_only +
            // WAL) so the probe sees the same journal-mode view of the DB.
            let mut conn = sqlx::sqlite::SqliteConnectOptions::new()
                .filename(index_path)
                .read_only(true)
                .journal_mode(sqlx::sqlite::SqliteJournalMode::Wal)
                .connect()
                .await?;
            let last: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar("PRAGMA data_version")
                .fetch_one(&mut conn)
                .await?;
            Ok::<_, sqlx::Error>(DataVersionProbe { conn, last })
        });
        match result {
            Ok(probe) => Some(probe),
            Err(e) => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    error = %e,
                    path = %index_path.display(),
                    "Failed to open data_version probe — falling back to identity-only staleness detection"
                );
                None
            }
        }
    }

fn open_readonly_small_roundtrip() {
        // open_readonly_small right-sizes the mmap/cache for reference
        // indexes. Verify it still reads back data written by a normal Store.
        use crate::embedder::Embedding;
        use crate::parser::{Chunk, ChunkType, Language};

        let dir = tempfile::TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let db_path = dir.path().join("index.db");

        // Build a small fixture index with a regular read-write store.
        {
            let store = Store::open(&db_path).unwrap();
            store.init(&ModelInfo::default()).unwrap();

            let content = "fn small() {}";
            let hash = blake3::hash(content.as_bytes()).to_hex().to_string();
            let chunk = Chunk {
                id: format!("small.rs:1:{}", &hash[..8]),
                file: std::path::PathBuf::from("small.rs"),
                language: Language::Rust,
                chunk_type: ChunkType::Function,
                name: "small".to_string(),
                signature: "fn small()".to_string(),
                content: content.to_string(),
                doc: None,
                line_start: 1,
                line_end: 1,
                byte_start: 0,
                content_hash: hash,
                canonical_hash: String::new(),
                parent_id: None,
                window_idx: None,
                parent_type_name: None,
                parser_version: 0,
            };
            // A unit-vector embedding of the store's configured dim.
            let mut v = vec![0.0f32; store.dim()];
            if !v.is_empty() {
                v[0] = 1.0;
            }
            let embedding = Embedding::new(v);
            store.upsert_chunk(&chunk, &embedding, Some(100)).unwrap();
        }

        // Re-open with the small constructor and confirm the fixture is visible.
        let ro = Store::open_readonly_small(&db_path)
            .expect("open_readonly_small should succeed on a populated index");

        ro.check_model_version()
            .expect("schema/model check should pass on small-mode open");

        let stats = ro.stats().expect("stats() should work on small-mode store");
        assert_eq!(
            stats.total_chunks, 1,
            "small-mode store must see the fixture chunk"
        );

        let chunks = ro
            .get_chunks_by_origin("small.rs")
            .expect("get_chunks_by_origin should work on small-mode store");
        assert_eq!(chunks.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(chunks[0].name, "small");
    }

impl TaskEntry {
    /// A fresh `working` entry, before insert. `progress` starts `{0, 0}`; the
    /// admission path stamps `total` before insert and clones the handle into
    /// the worker's params.
    fn new_working(id: TaskId, spawn_epoch: u64, ttl_secs: Option<u64>) -> TaskEntry {
        TaskEntry {
            id,
            status: AtomicU8::new(TaskStatus::Working as u8),
            result: Mutex::new(None),
            created_at_iso: now_rfc3339(),
            ttl_secs,
            spawn_epoch,
            retained_bytes: AtomicUsize::new(0),
            progress: Arc::new(ProgressCounters::default()),
        }
    }

    /// Stamp the admission-time denominator `total` (M) into the progress
    /// counters. Called BEFORE the entry is admitted (inserted), while the entry
    /// is still single-owner and unpollable, so a `tasks/get` between insert and
    /// worker-start reads the real M, never the `{0, 0}` default.
    pub(in crate::cli::batch) fn stamp_progress_total(&self, total: u64) {
        self.progress.total.store(total, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// A handle to the shared progress counters, cloned into the worker's
    /// `EvalCoreParams::progress` so `eval_core`'s `done` bumps land on the same
    /// atomics this entry's descriptor reads.
    pub(in crate::cli::batch) fn progress_handle(&self) -> Arc<ProgressCounters> {
        Arc::clone(&self.progress)
    }

    fn status(&self) -> TaskStatus {
        TaskStatus::from_u8(self.status.load(Ordering::Acquire))
    }

    /// Publish the terminal outcome. Fills the result slot FIRST, then flips
    /// `status` with `Release` so a reader that observes a terminal
    /// status via `load(Acquire)` always sees the filled slot. Write-once: a
    /// second publish (e.g. the drop handle after a normal publish, or a late
    /// duplicate) is ignored.
    pub(in crate::cli::batch) fn publish(&self, kind: TerminalKind, status: TaskStatus) {
        let bytes = kind.retained_bytes();
        {
            let mut slot = self.result.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
            if slot.is_some() {
                return;
            }
            *slot = Some(TerminalResult {
                kind,
                finished_at: Instant::now(),
                finished_at_iso: now_rfc3339(),
            });
        }
        self.retained_bytes.store(bytes, Ordering::Relaxed);
        // Flip status LAST, with Release, so `status.load(Acquire)` implies the
        // slot is filled.
        self.status.store(status as u8, Ordering::Release);
    }

    fn descriptor(&self) -> TaskDescriptor {
        // READ-ORDER PIN (seam-coherent join): load `status` (Acquire) FIRST,
        // then the progress counters. The worker's store order is the inverse —
        // it bumps the counters, then fills the result slot, then flips `status`
        // with `Release`. So a reader that observes a terminal `status` here has,
        // by happens-before, already synchronized-with every counter bump; the
        // subsequent counter load therefore sees the FINAL `done`. A single
        // descriptor can never pair a terminal status with a stale `done < total`.
        let status = self.status();
        // Progress read AFTER status. `Relaxed` is sound: the ordering guarantee
        // rides the `status` Acquire above, not these loads.
        let progress = Some(TaskProgress {
            done: self.progress.done.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            total: self.progress.total.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        });
        // `lastUpdatedAt` moves to the terminal instant once terminal; before
        // that it equals `createdAt`.
        let last_updated_at = if status.is_terminal() {
            self.result
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())
                .as_ref()
                .map(|t| t.finished_at_iso.clone())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| self.created_at_iso.clone())
        } else {
            self.created_at_iso.clone()
        };
        TaskDescriptor {
            task_id: self.id.as_str().to_string(),
            status,
            created_at: self.created_at_iso.clone(),
            last_updated_at,
            ttl_secs: self.ttl_secs,
            progress,
        }
    }

    /// GC predicate: a terminal task whose `terminal_at + ttl` has passed.
    /// Non-terminal and unlimited-ttl (`None`) entries are never reclaimed here.
    fn is_expired(&self, now: Instant) -> bool {
        if !self.status().is_terminal() {
            return false;
        }
        let Some(ttl) = self.ttl_secs else {
            return false;
        };
        let slot = self.result.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        match slot.as_ref() {
            Some(tr) => now.saturating_duration_since(tr.finished_at) > Duration::from_secs(ttl),
            // Terminal status but no slot yet (a torn read window) — keep it.
            None => false,
        }
    }
}

    let payload = match task_id_from_args(arguments) {

    };
    crate::cli::json_envelope::wrap_value(&payload)

    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        // Redact `task_id`: a `?descriptor` in a tracing call must not leak the
        // capability handle, same posture as `TaskId`'s Debug. The
        // wire response carries the id via explicit field access, not Debug.
        f.debug_struct("TaskDescriptor")
            .field("task_id", &"redacted")
            .field("status", &self.status)
            .field("created_at", &self.created_at)
            .field("last_updated_at", &self.last_updated_at)
            .field("ttl_secs", &self.ttl_secs)
            // Progress is `{done, total}` counts — no capability handle, safe to
            // render.
            .field("progress", &self.progress)
            .finish()
    }

impl TaskStore {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Arc<TaskStore> {
        Arc::new(TaskStore {
            tasks: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
            shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false)),
            job_seq: AtomicU64::new(0),
        })
    }

    /// The shutdown cancel token a worker threads into `EvalCoreParams::cancel`.
    pub(in crate::cli::batch) fn shutdown_token(&self) -> Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool> {
        Arc::clone(&self.shutdown)
    }

    /// Signal daemon shutdown so in-flight workers bail at their next per-query
    /// check. Idempotent.
    pub(crate) fn signal_shutdown(&self) {
        self.shutdown.store(true, Ordering::Release);
    }

    /// Next non-secret worker-thread job id.
    pub(in crate::cli::batch) fn next_job_seq(&self) -> u64 {
        self.job_seq.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    /// Shared cap predicate — the single source of truth for both the
    /// fast-reject probe and the authoritative admit.
    fn is_full(map: &HashMap<TaskId, Arc<TaskEntry>>) -> bool {
        if map.len() >= RETAINED_TASK_COUNT_CAP {
            return true;
        }
        let retained: usize = map
            .values()
            .map(|e| e.retained_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
            .sum();
        retained >= RETAINED_TASK_BYTES_CEILING
    }

    /// Non-mutating cap probe. Lets admission fast-reject BEFORE it reads a
    /// fixture, so a saturated store does no I/O and allocates nothing.
    pub(in crate::cli::batch) fn at_capacity(&self) -> bool {
        let map = self.tasks.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        Self::is_full(&map)
    }

    /// Mint a fresh `taskId` and build a `working` entry for it. Kept separate
    /// from insertion so the caller can stamp the epoch/ttl before committing.
    pub(in crate::cli::batch) fn new_entry(
        &self,
        spawn_epoch: u64,
        ttl_secs: Option<u64>,
    ) -> Arc<TaskEntry> {
        Arc::new(TaskEntry::new_working(
            TaskId::generate(),
            spawn_epoch,
            ttl_secs,
        ))
    }

    /// Authoritative admission: under the map lock, re-check the caps and insert
    /// the entry. Returns `false` (allocating nothing) at cap — the caller maps
    /// `false` to the opaque `Unavailable`, byte-identical to single-flight-busy
    /// . Insert-then-spawn ordering: the caller spawns the worker
    /// only after this returns `true`, and the worker's publish-on-drop handle
    /// self-heals a spawn-fail orphan to `failed`.
    pub(in crate::cli::batch) fn try_admit(&self, entry: Arc<TaskEntry>) -> bool {
        let mut map = self.tasks.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        if Self::is_full(&map) {
            return false;
        }
        map.insert(entry.id.clone(), entry);
        true
    }

    /// Snapshot an entry's wire-facing descriptor — used by admission to return
    /// the freshly created task without a map round-trip.
    pub(in crate::cli::batch) fn describe(&self, entry: &Arc<TaskEntry>) -> TaskDescriptor {
        entry.descriptor()
    }

    /// Non-blocking status/timestamps read (`tasks/get`).
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, id: &TaskId) -> TaskLookup {
        let entry = {
            let map = self.tasks.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
            map.get(id).map(Arc::clone)
        };
        match entry {
            Some(e) => TaskLookup::Found(e.descriptor()),
            None => TaskLookup::Gone,
        }
    }

    /// Terminal-result read (`tasks/result`). `current_epoch` is the live
    /// invalidation epoch the caller reads from its own view; a mismatch against
    /// the stamped `spawn_epoch` injects the staleness marker.
    pub(crate) fn result(&self, id: &TaskId, current_epoch: u64) -> TaskResultLookup {
        let entry = {
            let map = self.tasks.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
            map.get(id).map(Arc::clone)
        };
        let Some(entry) = entry else {
            return TaskResultLookup::Gone;
        };
        // Read status (Acquire) before the slot, per the publish ordering.
        if !entry.status().is_terminal() {
            return TaskResultLookup::Pending;
        }
        let kind = {
            let slot = entry.result.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
            match slot.as_ref() {
                Some(tr) => tr.kind.clone(),
                // Terminal status, empty slot: a torn read — retry, not error.
                None => return TaskResultLookup::Pending,
            }
        };
        let staleness = if entry.spawn_epoch != current_epoch {
            Some(StaleMeta {
                computed_at_epoch: entry.spawn_epoch,
                index_moved_since_run: true,
            })
        } else {
            None
        };
        TaskResultLookup::Ready { kind, staleness }
    }

    /// GC backstop (NOT the cap enforcer). Drops terminal entries past their
    /// `terminal_at + ttl`. `try_lock` so a busy map never blocks the accept
    /// loop; a skipped sweep is harmless because admission — not GC — bounds the
    /// store.
    pub(crate) fn sweep_expired(&self) {
        let now = Instant::now();
        let Ok(mut map) = self.tasks.try_lock() else {
            return;
        };
        map.retain(|_, entry| !entry.is_expired(now));
    }
}

fn task_timestamps_are_rfc3339() {
        let store = TaskStore::new();
        let entry = store.new_entry(0, Some(60));

        // Pre-terminal: `lastUpdatedAt` equals `createdAt`, both valid RFC3339.
        let d0 = entry.descriptor();
        chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&d0.created_at)
            .expect("createdAt must be a valid RFC3339 string");
        assert_eq!(
            d0.last_updated_at, d0.created_at,
            "pre-terminal lastUpdatedAt equals createdAt"
        );

        // A tick so the terminal stamp is observably distinct from creation.
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2));
        entry.publish(
            TerminalKind::ToolResult {
                value: serde_json::json!({"ok": true}),
                is_error: false,
            },
            TaskStatus::Completed,
        );

        // Terminal: both stamps valid RFC3339; lastUpdatedAt moved to the finish
        // instant (never before creation).
        let d1 = entry.descriptor();
        let created = chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&d1.created_at)
            .expect("terminal createdAt must be a valid RFC3339 string");
        let updated = chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&d1.last_updated_at)
            .expect("terminal lastUpdatedAt must be a valid RFC3339 string");
        assert!(
            updated >= created,
            "terminal lastUpdatedAt ({}) advances to the finish instant, not before createdAt ({})",
            d1.last_updated_at,
            d1.created_at
        );
        // The terminal stamp MOVED — it is the finish instant, not a frozen copy
        // of createdAt. Pins the `descriptor()` terminal branch (which cargo-
        // mutants could only replace wholesale, an unviable Default); the 2ms
        // tick above guarantees a distinct RFC3339 rendering.
        assert_ne!(
            d1.last_updated_at, d1.created_at,
            "terminal lastUpdatedAt must move to the finish instant, not stay == createdAt"
        );
    }

impl TaskStatus {
    fn from_u8(v: u8) -> TaskStatus {
        match v {
            1 => TaskStatus::Completed,
            2 => TaskStatus::Failed,
            3 => TaskStatus::Cancelled,
            // 0 and any unexpected byte read as the non-terminal state, which is
            // the safe default (a reader waits rather than reading an empty slot).
            _ => TaskStatus::Working,
        }
    }

    fn is_terminal(self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self, TaskStatus::Working)
    }

    /// The MCP wire string (`working`, not `in_progress`).
    pub(crate) fn as_wire(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            TaskStatus::Working => "working",
            TaskStatus::Completed => "completed",
            TaskStatus::Failed => "failed",
